post.description: Upload one capture segment from a linked device as multipart form data. Identity is the linked-device mTLS certificate. The body has one JSON `envelope` part plus repeated `files` parts. Envelope grammar is `core/crates/solstone-core/src/contract/schemas/protocol.schema.json` (required `day`, `segment`, `files`; optional `source`, `meta`; `stream` and `observer` are forbidden). Each multipart part is at most 64 MiB; the total request is at most 128 MiB.

parameters.description: Linked-device ingest protocol version. Must be 3. Values less than 3 are rejected with HTTP 426 Upgrade Required; values greater than 3 are rejected as unsupported. Identity is the linked-device mTLS certificate, not a request header.
parameters.name: X-Solstone-Protocol-Version

file_descriptors.description: One custody receipt per submitted file, returned only after the journal durably recorded the upload. A device proves custody of a file when its `sha256` and `size` equal the local file's and its `disposition` is `written` or `already_held`; `received_not_written` is never custody.

refused_files.description: Present only on folder-source uploads when one or more companion files failed per-file checking while valid events or files landed.

409.description: Held sidecar bytes conflict, the device's stream binding is refused, or a note window or screenshot is later than the journal's today (held on the device and sent again later).

413.description: Request exceeds the 128 MiB total-body limit.

500.description: Journal write or notification failed, or the owner removed the requested segment (`reason_code: segment_removed`, body `status: failed`). A device that knows `segment_removed` stops re-sending that segment.

503.description: The journal can't take this upload right now (body `status: retryable`). Hold it and send it again later.

folder.description: Watched-folder file activity and optional content files from a linked device. One upload carries one 5-minute window (`HHMMSS_300` on the journal's 300-second grid) for one folder (`meta.folder`), consisting of one `folder_<sha256>.jsonl` activity file and zero or more companion content parts referenced by `part` fields on lines in that activity file. Activity-only windows render deterministically to `talents/screen_text.md` with zero model passes; companion content files route by `kind_hint` (falling back to deterministic triage when absent or unrecognized).
folder.capability_rule: Send only to a journal whose `GET /api/system/status` lists `folder` in `capabilities`. Below that, hold folder uploads on the device until the paired journal lists it.
folder.window_grid: One segment per watched folder per 5-minute window (`HHMMSS_300` on the 300-second grid in each event's own offset). Each folder binds its own internal stream keyed by `meta.folder.id` so concurrent folders never collide.
folder.files: Exactly one `folder_<64 lowercase hex sha256>.jsonl` activity file whose filename hash equals SHA-256 of its UTF-8 bytes (<= 8 MiB, <= 5,000 lines, trailing newline), plus 0..63 companion content parts referenced by `part` fields on lines in that file. Companion part names must not use reserved journal names.
folder.per_file_checking: Broken companion files (hash mismatch, undecodable or oversized image, corrupt or encrypted PDF, invalid UTF-8 note, unsupported binary format) are refused by name in `refused_files` while valid activity events and companion files in the same window land (`200 OK`). When every item in an upload fails per-file checking and nothing lands, the journal answers `400` with `reason_code: folder_file_invalid` and `refused_files`.
folder.deleted: Each folder keeps a fail-closed received ledger keyed by `meta.folder.id` that outlives segment erase. Re-sending an already-received event, screenshot, photo, or document revision — including after the owner erased the segment or re-paired the device — answers `duplicate` without resurrecting deleted memories. An unreadable ledger answers `503 retryable`.

answers.meaning: Accepted into the folder's 5-minute segment. Check optional `refused_files` for any individual broken companion files.
answers.client_action: Mark landed items delivered. Any path listed in `refused_files` reached a terminal per-file refusal unless the file changes on disk.

answers.meaning: Every event and file in this upload was already received for this folder (including items the owner later erased).
answers.client_action: Mark delivered and do not resend.

answers.meaning: The envelope, `meta.folder`, activity JSONL, or part references break the contract.
answers.client_action: Do not resend the malformed upload as-is.

answers.meaning: Every item in the upload failed per-file checking (`refused_files` names each file and reason).
answers.client_action: Mark each named file refused until its bytes change.

answers.meaning: The window's day is later than the journal's today.
answers.client_action: Hold it and resend once the journal's day reaches it.

answers.meaning: The journal cannot take this upload right now (received ledger unreadable, PDF extractor unavailable, or busy).
answers.client_action: Hold it and retry with backoff.

answers.meaning: The journal could not finish the write.
answers.client_action: Hold it and retry with backoff.

screenshots.description: A screenshot the owner took, sent by the solstone app on the device that holds it. One upload carries one screenshot. It lands at its capture second in the sending device's screenshots stream, is made searchable the way a screen is, and is kept once across the owner's devices.
screenshots.capability_rule: Send only to a journal whose `GET /api/system/status` lists `screenshots` in `capabilities`. Below that, hold every screenshot on the device and send it once the paired journal lists it.
screenshots.files: Exactly one file per upload, named `screenshot_screen.<extension>` with an accepted extension in lowercase. No other file goes with it, and that name is refused under any other source.
screenshots.accepted_types_rule: The bytes must be the type the extension names. The journal accepts png, jpg, jpeg and webp, and refuses HEIC, HEIF, TIFF, GIF, PDF and every other type because it can't decode them. Send an accepted type exactly as the platform saved it. A type outside those is converted to PNG on the device, keeping its metadata, and sent as png.

size_limit.rule: At most 64 MiB, the part limit for every upload (larger is refused with `multipart_part_too_large`), and at most 100,000,000 pixels by the image's own header (larger is refused with `screenshot_invalid`).

screenshots.identity: A screenshot is the SHA-256 of its exact bytes, computed by the journal; the device sends no id. Send an accepted type exactly as the platform saved it: do not re-encode, resize, crop, rotate or strip its metadata. A type outside png, jpg, jpeg and webp is converted to PNG on the device, keeping its metadata, and then the identity is the hash of that PNG. The same bytes from a second device, or sent again after a re-scan, a turn-back-on or a re-pair, are the same screenshot and are answered `duplicate`.
screenshots.capture_time: `meta.screenshot.captured_at` is the moment it was taken, RFC 3339 with the UTC offset in force where it was taken (`Z` means `+00:00`). It comes from the platform's own record of the screenshot or from the file (its embedded date or modification time), never from a model, and `meta.screenshot.taken_from` says which (`platform` or `file`). The envelope's `day` (`YYYYMMDD`) and `segment` (`HHMMSS_1`) are that moment's date and clock time in its own offset, so the screenshot lands at the minute it was taken.
screenshots.device: The device is the linked device that sends the upload, by its mTLS identity; no field names it. The screenshot lands in that device's screenshots stream and is labelled with the device's name as the journal shows it. A screenshot already received from another device keeps the label of the device that sent it first.
screenshots.deleted: The journal remembers every screenshot this source has received, and that memory outlives a delete. A screenshot the owner deleted from the journal is answered `duplicate` when a device sends it again, from any device and after any re-scan. The owner bringing the same file in through the Import page or a share is a re-import and arrives as new data; that path is not this source.

answers.client_action: Hold it and send it again once the journal's day has reached it.

answers.client_action: Hold it and send it again later, with backoff. A resend of the same bytes is never kept twice.

answers.client_action: As for every other source: hold it and follow the pairing contract.

get.description: Return segment upload history for one day as a protocol-version-3 collection envelope. The physical locator is the day, stream directory, and exact segment-directory basename. `key` is that basename unless this response repeats the basename; repeated basenames use `{basename}~{stream}`, then `~2`, `~3`, and so on, and those items also carry `segment` (the directory basename) and `stream`. `original_key` records only an upload remap of the requested key and does not identify a stream. A within-segment effective-name clash remains `ambiguous_segment_file_name`. Per-file `status` is `present`, `processed`, or `missing`. `submitted_name` appears only when the stored filename differs from the submitted one.
